email.scenario: Last week my photo backup app sent a storage-limit warning that I didn't notice until today. Because the storage stayed full, the app automatically deleted several months of photos from my phone to make room, and I'm told the cloud recovery window for those files closes in 48 hours.
email.subject: Urgent: Recovery Window Closing for Auto-Deleted Photos
bullets: Explain that you missed the storage warning notification and your local photos were automatically deleted as a result.
Request an extension of the recovery window before the files are permanently deleted.
Ask whether opening a support ticket would help expedite the recovery process.

academicDiscussion.professorPost: Content moderation on major platforms remains largely opaque: users rarely learn exactly why a post was removed or which rule it violated. Some argue that publishing the specific criteria behind moderation algorithms would make platforms more accountable and help users trust removal decisions, while others worry that revealing those details would let bad actors reverse-engineer the system and manipulate it. Should platforms be required to publish the specific criteria their moderation algorithms use? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Priya
studentPosts.post: I think platforms should publish their criteria. Right now users have no way to know if a removal was fair or arbitrary, and that secrecy breeds distrust. Clear published standards would let people appeal decisions with actual evidence instead of guessing, and it would pressure platforms to apply their own rules consistently.

studentPosts.name: Marcus
studentPosts.post: I get Priya's point about trust, but publishing exact criteria hands bad actors a manual for gaming the system. Spammers and harassers would just tweak their posts to slip under whatever threshold is public. Platforms could instead publish general principles without exposing the technical details that make manipulation possible.
